context: A scrollable heatmap table showing test coverage percentages for 26 D3.js skills across 16 test dimensions, with a single-hue sequential (Blues) color scale, numeric cell labels, sortable columns, palette switcher, and hover tooltips.
first_impression: Clean and readable — the monotone blue scale and inline numbers keep a 416-cell matrix from feeling overwhelming.
what_works: Single-hue sequential palette avoids categorical color confusion and encodes magnitude intuitively; numeric values printed inside each cell let viewers read precise coverage without relying solely on color estimation. Sort controls help surface patterns (gaps, high performers) on demand.
what_doesnt: The 70vh scrollable container truncates the table so rows at the top and bottom can't be compared simultaneously, fragmenting holistic skill-level comparison and loading working memory; no per-row total column means viewers must mentally average 16 values to assess a skill's overall coverage rather than reading one summary figure.
